name: McKenzie and Parker’s rigid-plate kinematics
description: McKenzie and Parker modeled the motion of rigid plates on a spherical Earth and applied it to North Pacific tectonics.

impact.note: Made the existing idea of a mobile sea floor quantitative for earth scientists, alongside similar work by others; plate-motion modelling and modern tectonics build on it.

date.basis: Year of the dated publication, or a broad historian-estimated composition interval; no first discovery claimed.

events.statement: McKenzie and Parker published their North Pacific plate-motion analysis in 1967.

evidence.supports: The abstract and metadata describe the 1967 North Pacific rigid-plate treatment.
The USGS account relates the 1967–68 plate framework to Hess seafloor spreading and magnetic evidence.

caveats: The paper is one contribution to a multi-author 1960s synthesis. A publisher abstract and historical synthesis were inspected, not the complete 1967 paper; rigid plates are an approximation. The reviewed historical narrative supports a broad sequence, but the full 1967 paper was not inspected to substantiate a direct dependence on Hess. The publisher’s reference list does cite Hess’s 1962 contribution, but the context of that citation is unavailable from the abstract.

research.note: Independent reading checked the source-supported event and chronology. Grain and other unreviewed facets remain provisional.

links.statement: The paper cites Hess’s 1962 contribution, and a later USGS synthesis connects seafloor spreading to the broader plate-tectonics development; the direct role of Hess’s work in this paper remains to be checked.
